faq: How is this different from Amazon Ads setup?
Amazon Ads is a first setup with one or two reviews. PPC management goes deeper: keyword research, a rebuilt campaign structure and tuning rounds, aimed at accounts already spending money on ads.
What do you need to start?
Reporting and campaign access in Amazon Ads, your product costs or target margin, and a list of the products you most want to push. Spend data from the last 60 days helps us.
We cannot name a number honestly. It depends on your price, margin, reviews and competition. We set a target together, work toward it step by step and show real figures.
Do you bid on competitor brands?
Only where Amazon allows it. We never use trademarked names in listing copy, and any competitor targeting is limited to the product targeting that Amazon Ads offers, only with your approval.
desc:
Amazon PPC management and keyword tuning make sure your ad money goes to searches that can pay you back. Ecom Swift LLC audits your campaigns, researches keywords, rebuilds the structure, sets bids from your margins and tunes them over the sprint.

## What is Amazon PPC management?

Amazon PPC management is the ongoing work of running pay-per-click campaigns well. It includes choosing keywords, grouping them into campaigns, setting bids and budgets, removing wasteful terms and reading reports. Each click costs money, so every decision about a bid or a keyword affects your profit.

This service is for accounts that already run ads. If you have no campaigns yet, a first-time ads setup is a better starting point.

## Why campaigns drift and waste money

Campaigns do not stay efficient on their own. A keyword that sold well in spring may attract clicks and no orders in autumn. Broad and auto campaigns collect irrelevant searches, and without negative keywords those searches keep costing money. Campaigns that mix many products, match types and goals in one place make it hard to see what works.

Many sellers also set bids by feel. A bid above what the margin supports can turn every order into a loss, while a bid set too low means the ad never shows. The fix is to base bids on what a sale is worth to you.

## How tuning affects efficiency

Search term reports show what shoppers typed before clicking. Reading them lets you add terms that convert, stop terms that waste budget and move winners into tighter campaigns. Splitting campaigns by match type means you can give different bids to exact, phrase and broad terms.

This work lowers wasted spend and shows where budget helps. It does not set demand or price, and results also depend on listing quality, reviews and competition. We follow Amazon Ads policies and cannot promise a target cost of sales or a revenue figure.

## What a well-run PPC account includes

- An audit of existing campaigns, budgets, bids and settings.
- Keyword research for each product, based on real shopper phrases.
- Campaigns grouped by product and match type.
- Bids set from your price, costs and margin.
- Negative keywords added to block irrelevant searches.
- Budget caps that suit your cash and goals.
- Tuning rounds that change bids and budgets using fresh data.
- A review of the search term report with notes on each decision.
- A plain summary and a plan for the next month.

## How we manage your campaigns

We start with an audit inside your advertising console. We list campaigns, find where money is spent without orders, and record the starting position. For the products in scope we research keywords and decide which belong in which campaign.

We then rebuild the structure where needed, set bids from your margins and add negative keywords. During the sprint we tune bids and budgets and read the search term report for fresh ideas. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages grow from an audit with the largest wastes fixed, to a rebuilt structure with keyword research, to a larger range with two tuning rounds and a thirty-day plan. Ad spend stays between your account and Amazon.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Share your costs so bids can reflect your real margin.
- Give each tuning round enough days of data.
- Keep stock levels healthy while ads run.
- Review the search term report on a regular schedule.
- Keep a log of changes and the reasons for them.

**Avoid:**
- Bidding on competitors' brand names.
- Raising every bid at once to chase more traffic.
- Leaving poor keywords running because they were once useful.
- Running ads on listings with weak images or low stock.
- Judging a campaign after a single day.

## Who this is for

This service suits a seller whose ad bills keep growing while orders stay flat. It also suits a brand that built its campaigns early and now has a tangled structure. An owner with several products can use the keyword research to give each one its own focused campaign.

## What we need from you

Please send your product costs, your target margin and any keywords or products you want left alone. You invite us as a user in your advertising console and Seller Central with the permissions needed to edit campaigns. We never ask for your password.
